## What this does

Plumbing, not part of the method itself. These append one more field to a
[`Rec`](rec_ctor.qmd) output line under construction: `s` for raw text,
`name` for a site/species/time code, `x` for `n` blank characters (column
padding/spacing), `i` for a right-aligned whole number, `f` for a
right-aligned decimal number. `writeln` finishes the line and writes it
out. Chaining these calls is what produces each row of, for example, the
sample-statistics or rescaled-frequency output tables — the Rust
equivalent of the original's fixed-format `WRITE` statements.

### `Rec::s`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__s"}
    pub fn s(&mut self, s: &str) -> &mut Self {
        self.buf.extend_from_slice(s.as_bytes());
        self
    }
```

### `Rec::name`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__name"}
    pub fn name(&mut self, n: &Name) -> &mut Self {
        self.buf.extend_from_slice(n);
        self
    }
```

### `Rec::x`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__x"}
    pub fn x(&mut self, n: usize) -> &mut Self {
        self.buf.extend(std::iter::repeat(BLANK).take(n));
        self
    }
```

### `Rec::i`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__i"}
    pub fn i(&mut self, v: i64, w: usize) -> &mut Self {
        self.s(&ifmt(v, w));
        self
    }
```

### `Rec::f`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__f"}
    pub fn f(&mut self, v: f32, w: usize, d: usize) -> &mut Self {
        self.s(&ffmt(v, w, d));
        self
    }
```

### `Rec::writeln`

```{.rust filename="src/lib.rs" tangle="lib__Rec__writeln"}
    pub fn writeln<W: Write>(&self, w: &mut W) {
        w.write_all(&self.buf).unwrap();
        w.write_all(b"\n").unwrap();
    }
```
